- If sentiment is positive (≥0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3), model often underestimates drops; adjust downward bias or add early correction factor.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply lagged correction or cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day mean by 2–5% in bullish sentiment periods; apply mean reversion bias toward historical 18-day average.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., 0.38 → 1.00 → 0.38), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast curve or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to “late correction” bias — true values often dip after 15–20 days; adjust for delayed mean reversion or add 10–15 day decay factor.
